key_insight: Replacing abstract language prompts with explicit points of physical contact (Contact-Anchored Policies, CAP) yields more concrete, robust utility models for manipulation. Structuring policies as a modular library of contact-conditioned utility models enables reliable, reusable robot behaviors.
problem_solved: Language conditioning is often too abstract to convey the concrete, spatial and force-related information needed for robust robot manipulation; CAP addresses this gap by conditioning behavior on explicit contact points in space.
method: Introduce Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP): condition policy selection and utility estimation on spatial contact points rather than textual prompts.
Structure CAP as a modular library of utility models—each module maps contact-conditioned sensory inputs to utility estimates or actions—allowing reuse across embodiments and tasks.
Use contact locations as grounding signals during training and inference to produce more physically accurate, transferable manipulation strategies.
impact: CAP provides a practical way to ground high-level intent in concrete physical signals, improving robustness and reusability of manipulation policies for researchers and engineers building real-world robot systems.

paper_title: Contact-Anchored Policies: Contact Conditioning Creates Strong Robot Utility Models
paper_authors: Zichen Jeff Cui, Omar Rayyan, Haritheja Etukuru, Bowen Tan, Zavier Andrianarivo
